effort: Brake for an obtuse exit and accept force after crossover and curved approaches.
brief: E2 uses a planned 135-degree running cut. Low split-stance rebounds support staggered ankle force; a drop-step stop isolates a new receiving base, crossover and curved stops address different incoming paths, and a low rotational bound coordinates foot/hip orientation before landing.
marker: For E2, record early braking before the cone, a controlled plant and two steps along the 135-degree return diagonal; distinguish a controlled sharper cut from an uncontrolled pivot or loop.
readiness: An obtuse angle increases the redirection demand even with a short approach. Use lower entry intent until the athlete demonstrates the required positions; the first attempts count. No athlete response from Class 6 has been reported.
space: E2/E3/E5 require a measured 8 m × 6 m bay, with the return diagonal, curved route and tangent stop individually cleared. For the 135-degree task, the exit and stop head back diagonally, not into the incoming athlete or queue. Other work can follow a cleared lane axis.

drills.name: Split-Stance Pogo
drills.execution: Feet stay in a short staggered stance; make two very low ankle-driven rebounds, then reset and swap lead stance.
drills.job: Produce rapid ankle force from the unequal foot positions often present around a sharper plant.
drills.layout: Centre of lane with stable staggered base; no stance switch in flight.
drills.difference: Fixed staggered bilateral support rather than parallel-foot lateral or forward/back line travel.
drills.regress: Reduce height/cadence if one knee collapses or the stance widens in flight.
drills.exposure: 2 bilateral landings per stance attempt, 4 total.

drills.name: 135-Degree Running Cut
drills.execution: Use a controlled 1.5 m approach, brake before the cone and turn 135 degrees into a 1.5 m diagonal return; stop over 2 m.
drills.job: Main early-braking practice when the exit demands substantial reversal of the incoming momentum.
drills.layout: Mark the return diagonal 45 degrees off the straight-back line. Clear the 3.5 m exit/stop, 2 m straight-ahead abort and side margins; mirror separately.
drills.difference: An obtuse return diagonal differs from the 45-degree continuation, square corner and full 180-degree shuttle; the distinct braking demand justifies the angle-specific drill.
drills.regress: Lower entry intent first if the turn becomes a locked-foot pivot; retain the declared route rather than substituting a prior drill.

drills.name: Drop-Step Decel Cone Box
drills.execution: From athletic stance, make one quick drop step into a cone-marked rear diagonal base within 0.5 m, reorient the other foot as it unloads and hold 2 s. No crossover or sprint.
drills.job: Own the receiving base for a rear-diagonal redirection before a running exit is demanded.
drills.layout: A 3 m × 3 m clear area; cones mark the final stance, not a multi-corner course.
drills.difference: One rapid step into a terminal stop; the earlier drop-step drill continued through a crossover into running.
drills.regress: Use a smaller step if the knee twists or the stance becomes too wide.
drills.exposure: 1 rapid weight-acceptance stop, 0 running cuts; 0.5 m ground travel ceiling.

drills.name: Crossover Run to Stick
drills.execution: Travel laterally with crossover running steps for 2 m, then brake over 2 m into a balanced staggered stop and hold 2 s.
drills.job: Control incoming momentum after crossed-leg running instead of only after a square shuffle.
drills.layout: Face obliquely across the lane, travel along its length from 2 to 4 and stop by 6; mirror from 8 toward 6 and stop by 4.
drills.difference: A moving crossover gait terminates in braking; stationary crossover starts and crossover-to-bound have different contact sequences.
drills.regress: Shorten strides if legs tangle or the torso keeps rotating during the stop.
drills.exposure: 1 terminal braking episode, no prescribed jump.

drills.name: Curved Run Decel
drills.execution: Run a quarter-circle arc of 1.5 m radius at controlled speed, leave on its tangent and stop within 2 m; do not plant-cut at the arc end.
drills.job: Reduce momentum after a curved entry while controlling lean and pelvis position.
drills.layout: Arc travel is about 2.36 m; mark the radius and tangent stop within the bay. Keep inside/outside margins empty.
drills.difference: Distributed curving entry then terminal deceleration, rather than a straight entry or a discrete cone cut.
drills.regress: Lower arc speed if the athlete leans from the waist or steps across the feet.
drills.exposure: 1 terminal braking episode; curved heading change is continuous and not logged as a planted cut.

drills.name: Rotational Bound to Stick
drills.execution: Push from one leg, make a low short bound within 0.4 m while rotating 90 degrees, land on the opposite leg and hold 2 s.
drills.job: Align hips and landing foot in the air before accepting a redirected force.
drills.layout: 3 m × 3 m clear landing area, no approach run and no height target; mirror takeoff/landing legs.
drills.difference: Unilateral opposite-leg landing with an airborne quarter-turn, distinct from the bilateral quarter-turn jump and non-rotating lateral bound.
drills.regress: Reduce rotation/flight distance if the foot and pelvis arrive out of alignment; log the changed angle.

light.job: Control rotation of the pelvis over the planted leg in the obtuse exit.
Maintain foot-edge control during the obtuse plant without adding adductor pre-fatigue.

strength.job: Frontal-plane loading supports the rear-diagonal push.
Maintain knee/hip force through a lowered sharper-cut plant.
Maintain hip-hinge capacity without increasing volume as entry shape changes.
Maintain adductor support under a changed force direction.
Bent-knee ankle force supports the low plant and redirected push.

previous_review: Class 6 prescribed twelve locomotor attempts and six travel reversals, with only two bilateral flight landings. No actual control or recovery data is available.
progression: Use a new exit angle and entry shapes with controlled speed; reduce true running cuts to four rather than increasing speed and cut count together. Keep rotational flight very small and conditional on alignment.
strength_progression: Return to the reduced familiar Class 5 strength pattern: one round each, target reserve unchanged. No load increase is assumed from the written Class 6.
audit: Counted curved heading change separately from planted direction changes. Limited the rotational bound to two total landings and replaced the extra adductor-light set with easy ankle eversion so Copenhagen work is not preceded by redundant adductor loading.
next: Next class emphasizes smooth curved entries and consolidation of load; review actual curved braking and obtuse-plant control first.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Control rotation of the pelvis over the planted leg in the obtuse exit.

light_entries.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
light_entries.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
light_entries.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
light_entries.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
light_entries.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.
light_entries.job: Maintain foot-edge control during the obtuse plant without adding adductor pre-fatigue.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Frontal-plane loading supports the rear-diagonal push.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: Maintain knee/hip force through a lowered sharper-cut plant.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Maintain hip-hinge capacity without increasing volume as entry shape changes.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor support under a changed force direction.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Bent-knee ankle force supports the low plant and redirected push.
